title: Classification systems
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: How do scientists decide which group an animal belongs to?
What is the difference between a species name and a genus name?
Can you show me how a cladogram helps us understand evolution?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how scientists group living things. This grouping system is called taxonomy. It helps us organize the amazing variety of life on Earth.

items: Taxonomy is the science of classification.
It organizes living things into groups.
These groups help us understand relationships.

explain.say: The Linnaean system uses ranks to classify organisms. These ranks go from Kingdom down to Species. Think of it like a set of nested boxes.

explain.say: Every species gets a unique two-part scientific name. This is called binomial nomenclature. The first part is the genus, and the second is the species.
A cladogram is a diagram showing evolutionary relationships. It groups organisms based on shared derived characteristics. These shared traits suggest common ancestry.
Consider the classification of humans and chimpanzees. They share a common ancestor, which is shown by grouping them together on a cladogram. This shows close relatedness.
A common mistake is mixing up the genus and species names. Remember that the genus name always starts with a capital letter. Always write the whole name in italics.

items: Always use italics for scientific names.

draw.text: Italics: Always write names in italics

faq.q: What is the difference between a genus and a family?
faq.a: A genus is a group of closely related species. A family is a broader group that contains several genera. You might ask what a genus represents or what a family encompasses.
asks: How are genera related to families?

faq.q: Do all organisms on a cladogram have to be alive today?
faq.a: No, the cladogram shows evolutionary paths, so some points represent extinct ancestors. You could also ask what the root of a cladogram means or if fossils are shown.
asks: What does the root of the tree mean?
Are extinct species shown on a cladogram?

faq.q: Why do scientists use scientific names instead of common names?
faq.a: Common names can change or mean different things in different places. Scientific names provide a universal, unambiguous way to identify any species globally. You might ask why names change or what universal naming means.
asks: Why are scientific names better than local names?
What is the purpose of binomial nomenclature?

faq.q: How many ranks are there in the Linnaean system?
faq.a: There are several major ranks, including Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species. You can also ask for the full list of taxonomic ranks or which rank is the broadest.
asks: What is the full hierarchy of life?
Can you list all the taxonomic ranks?

faq.q: What does a shared derived characteristic mean in a cladogram?
faq.a: It means a trait that evolved once in a common ancestor and was passed down to all descendants. Finding these traits helps scientists map out evolutionary relationships. You might ask what a synapomorphy is or how to identify shared traits.
asks: How do we know two things are related?

facts: The Linnaean system organizes life into hierarchical ranks.
Binomial nomenclature uses two parts: genus and species.
A cladogram illustrates evolutionary relationships based on shared traits.
The scientific name must be written in italics.

quiz.say: A scientist names a new species Canis familiaris. Which rank is Canis?
quiz.why: The first part of the two-part name is always the genus, which is capitalized.

wrong.1: This is incorrect because species is the second, lowercase part of the name.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because family is a higher rank than the genus.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because kingdom is the broadest rank, much larger than a genus.

quiz.say: If two species share a trait like feathers, what does this suggest on a cladogram?
quiz.why: Shared traits suggest that the species inherited that trait from a recent common ancestor.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because shared traits in biology are usually evidence of shared history.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because that would be called convergent evolution, not shared ancestry on a cladogram.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because evolution does not imply one species directly taught the trait to another.
